contexts.description: The server-side REST client layer that all console modules use to talk to the Brainiac binary. api.ts is the single authorised fetch wrapper (server-only, bearer token from env); api-schema.d.ts is generated from openapi.json; governance-api.ts contains governance-specific helpers; format/seeded/types are shared utilities. Also includes the /api/status proxy route and the demo-fallback shim that returns fixture data when the live API is unavailable.
contexts.name: api-client

contexts.description: The navigational and layout skeleton of the entire console SPA: root and console layouts, the chrome wrapper, global CSS, and the ModuleBoundary that lazy-mounts each feature module. The src/components directory supplies shared Nav, Skeleton, Divider, and error boundary primitives; src/design owns the route registry (which routes are public vs protected) and the design theme.
contexts.name: app-shell

contexts.description: Handles Firebase-backed authentication: login and signup pages collect credentials, server actions validate against Firebase Admin SDK and set a session cookie, and the middleware enforces the public/protected surface split on every request. The lib/auth module owns session validation and the SESSION_COOKIE constant consumed by middleware.
contexts.name: auth-shell

contexts.description: Provides the deterministic data-generation layer for Brainiac's scale evaluation corpus ('Meridian Bank'). `bank-org.mjs` declares the org topology — teams, hub entities with cross-team dialects, domain claims, contradiction seams, and cross-cutting practices — as pure data so the shape is readable independently of the generation machinery. `gen-bank-corpus.mjs` turns that data into YAML fixture files (1,200+ memories, entity merge sets, contradiction cases, QA/leak/temporal gold slices, and extraction transcripts) that feed `cargo run -- eval`. `seed-bank-docs.mjs` reads the seeded corpus back out of Postgres and bulk-inserts ~1,050 knowledge-base pages (entity pages, topic pages, runbooks, post-mortems, ADRs, process pages, onboarding) so the KB layer runs under realistic document load without invoking the compose pipeline.
contexts.name: bank-corpus-tooling

contexts.description: All project-level configuration and observability instrumentation for the console: TypeScript and PostCSS compiler settings, the Vitest test runner config, Dockerfile for container builds, Next.js instrumentation hooks (server + edge), and Sentry error-monitoring config for both server and edge runtimes. The server-only stub ensures server modules can't be accidentally imported client-side in tests.
contexts.name: build-config

contexts.api_surface: Consumes: POST /v1/memories/search, POST /v1/memories, GET /v1/sources/:id, GET /v1/docs, GET /v1/library/standards, POST /v1/library/standards/propose, POST /v1/library/skills/propose, GET /v1/library/skills, POST /v1/library/usage, POST /v1/tokens
contexts.description: The ChainSonar field test is a realistic end-to-end harness that deploys three simulated developer agents (new-feature, refactor, UI-scaling) against the live ChainSonar codebase to surface design gaps, bugs, and feature opportunities in Brainiac's Memory, Library, and Knowledge Base modules. It provisions a scoped multi-user org via `setup.mjs`, routes every Brainiac call through an instrumented `bx.mjs` CLI that records timing and outcome to JSONL logs, then aggregates results into a findings report via `report.mjs`. Key dependencies are the Brainiac REST API and the external ChainSonar Next.js repository; agent briefs in `agents/` drive the three isolated git-worktree sessions.
contexts.name: chainsonar-field-test

contexts.description: Pure domain math and type definitions with no I/O or database dependencies. Implements temporal validity windows, rank fusion (RRF), vector/BM25 scoring, cross-encoder reranking, health metrics, PII redaction, and the canonical Principal/Memory/Document types shared by every crate. Being IO-free means all logic here is unit-tested without Postgres or an LLM.
contexts.name: core-algorithms

contexts.description: Establishes the foundational Postgres schema: org/team/user tenancy, the memories table with three-tier visibility, the knowledge graph (entities/edges/entity_links), governance tables (promotions/contradictions), the pgmq-shaped job queue, and the embedding-versions side-table pattern that allows zero-downtime model swaps. Also adds early operational extensions: worker-read grants, API tokens, memory feedback/resolution, language-aware FTS, canonical embedding consolidation, canonical aliases, pipeline-run stats, and the first HNSW ANN index. Row-level security policies enforcing `app.org_id`/`app.user_id` per transaction are defined here and are load-bearing for every later query path.
contexts.name: core-schema-migrations

contexts.description: Renders the organisation's memory knowledge graph as an interactive visualisation — a star-chart and depth-of-field view let operators explore how canonical memory clusters are connected. The cortex-data module fetches canonical node summaries; useCanonicalDetail loads individual node details via the canonical API route; the analytics module surfaces aggregate usage metrics alongside the graph.
contexts.name: cortex-graph

contexts.api_surface: reads fixture/seeded data only — no live API calls
contexts.description: Serves two public (unauthenticated) surfaces: the /demo route mounts a read-only console on the synthetic Meridian fixture org so prospects can explore the product without signing up; the /pitch route is a rich competitive evidence deck with diagrams, evidence matrices, and a balance-sheet layout. Both surfaces use seeded fixture data and the demo-fallback shim rather than the live org API.
contexts.name: demo-pitch

contexts.api_surface: docs endpoints via api-client; server actions in actions.ts
contexts.description: Powers the AI-generated document wiki: operators can read, approve revisions, and edit sections of auto-generated docs. DocReader renders markdown with Mermaid diagrams; SectionEditor handles inline edits; the tree module builds a navigation hierarchy from the flat document list; the docs module entry and [slug] route expose the docs surface inside the console.
contexts.name: docs-editor

contexts.description: The golden-fixture eval harness (Meridian suite) that regression-gates every retrieval and pipeline change: profiles cover retrieval (NDCG/MRR/Recall, RLS leak = 0), resolution (B³/pairwise clustering), contradiction detection, divergence, extraction recall, document composition, drift, and a backend grid bake-off. The fixtures crate loads and validates the YAML fixture tree for referential integrity before any benchmark run; a loader error kills CI before a corrupt fixture can pollute a baseline.
contexts.name: eval-quality-gate

contexts.description: Covers the three governance surfaces: the review worklist where operators approve or reject pending memory submissions, the dispute bench where contradictory memories are adjudicated, and the audit ledger that records every governance decision. Operators act through server actions that POST decisions back to the Brainiac API; the onboard request routes handle approval of new-agent join requests.
contexts.name: governance-worklist

contexts.description: Allows operators to submit new content into the Brainiac pipeline and monitor its processing status in real time. The SubmitBox accepts URLs or text; useIngestFeed polls the SSE feed route; AirlockView shows quarantined items awaiting review while ManifestView shows the full processing manifest. The API routes proxy ingest and feed requests to the Brainiac server.
contexts.name: ingest-monitor

contexts.description: The async worker chain that turns raw source text into governed knowledge: extract (LLM → raw memories + entities + relations), resolve (entity clustering), contradict (conflict detection), compose (document synthesis), plus sweeps for re-embedding, library mining, practice divergence detection, and OKF ingest. A single pipeline_principal scopes all writes; a shared worker loop drains the ingest queue stage by stage.
contexts.name: ingestion-pipeline

contexts.description: Manages API key lifecycle (create, preview, revoke) and project/repository registration that scopes memory access per codebase. Keys are created via the keys API routes which proxy to Brainiac; projects can be linked to one or more repos; the ops/SweepControl surface lets operators trigger and monitor background sweep jobs associated with a project.
contexts.name: keys-projects

contexts.api_surface: health and KB endpoints via api-client
contexts.description: Visualises the health and completeness of the organisation's knowledge base: KnowledgeHealth shows per-memory age decay curves and coverage gaps; the Observatory surface gives a high-level dashboard of KB freshness; the kb module renders the KB export page with projection diagrams and a rotation curve illustrating how memory coverage evolves over time.
contexts.name: knowledge-health

contexts.description: Extends the schema across three feature milestones: operational intelligence (source idempotency key, knowledge-health snapshots, memory facets, practice-divergence detection, sweep schedules), the document/KB layer (document pages as compiled projections over canonical memories, delete-policy tombstoning, KB publishing targets, compose-backoff tracking), and early platform features (identity federation via 0022, memory titles, raw-TTL sweeps, per-document read events, feedback resolution notes, digest-kind enumeration, and the Library substrate tables for standards and mining proposals). RLS and grants are added incrementally with each new org-scoped table.
contexts.name: knowledge-health-document-migrations

contexts.description: Pushes the org's knowledge base outward to external targets (Confluence, Git, OKF) in a one-way, health-gated, RLS-respecting flow. Only org-visible documents may leave; credentials are never stored in the database (only env-var references). Implements the Publisher trait with per-target adapters plus shared page rendering and bundle-level artifact generation (index.md, log.md).
contexts.name: knowledge-publish

contexts.description: Hosts the org skills catalog (agent-callable skills that agents can invoke) and the public-facing library page that explains the Brainiac layered-knowledge model. The library page renders illustrated sections (anatomy, layers, drift, status ladder) that double as onboarding documentation; the skills module lets operators browse and adopt available skills with server-action-backed adopt/revoke flows.
contexts.name: library-catalog

contexts.description: Covers the later platform milestones: Library normative layer completion (standards pages, skill proposals, list indexes), the Projects axis (repo whitelist, onboarding pairings, project stamping on memories/documents, path-prefix routing, per-project RLS isolation, OKF publish targets), quality and traceability improvements (revision faithfulness scores, divergence-axis labels, divergence identity attribution, contradiction sibling-lookup index), and the demand/retrieval intelligence layer (retrieval events ledger, extraction cache, knowledge-gaps table that turns unanswered questions into actionable work items). Also includes the migrations README documenting append-only rules and sequence-number conventions.
contexts.name: library-projects-retrieval-migrations

contexts.api_surface: External: OpenAI /chat/completions, Anthropic Messages API, Google Gemini generateContent, AWS Bedrock, Vertex AI
contexts.description: BYOM (Bring Your Own Model) abstraction layer that exposes a single ChatProvider trait implemented by OpenAI-compatible endpoints (Qwen/DashScope, Azure, Groq, DeepSeek, Ollama), Anthropic Messages API, Google Gemini, AWS Bedrock, and Google Vertex AI. Resilience (retry/timeout) and fire-and-forget LightTrack telemetry are shared across all providers; per-stage model overrides compose via ProviderRouter.
contexts.name: llm-provider-gateway

contexts.description: Provides the operator UI for browsing, searching, and inspecting the organisation's stored memories. The Archive table lists all memories with column filters and full-text search; MemoryInspector renders the detail panel. Data is fetched from the Brainiac REST API (memories endpoint) via the server-only api client, with pagination state managed by archive-index helpers.
contexts.name: memory-archive

contexts.api_surface: GET /health, POST /v1/memories, POST /v1/memories/search; MCP stdio tools: memory_search, memory_context, memory_add, entity_lookup, knowledge_propose, memory_feedback, memory_provenance
contexts.description: The axum HTTP server binary entry point, MCP stdio transport, bearer-token auth, OpenAPI schema generation, and the health/memories REST surface. Every handler resolves the caller's principal before touching data; the MCP loop is a pure handle_message function testable without a process. The admin pool (RLS-bypassing) is provisioned here for the two legitimate bypasses: org-true analytics and self-serve provisioning.
contexts.name: server-api-core

contexts.api_surface: GET /v1/docs, GET /v1/docs/{slug}, GET /v1/library/standards, GET /v1/library/skills/{slug}, POST /v1/library/adopt, GET /v1/reviews/promotions, POST /v1/onboard, GET /v1/projects, POST /v1/sweeps, GET /v1/alerts
contexts.description: All domain-specific HTTP handlers beyond the core memory surface: knowledge-base document reads, library standards/skills distribution, org onboarding and provisioning, project management, divergence sweeps, alerts, console proxy, and demand tracking. Every route resolves a bearer principal and runs under a scoped RLS transaction; the library surface enforces adopt-only serving and per-team (never per-person) usage telemetry.
contexts.name: server-feature-modules

contexts.api_surface: standards and divergence endpoints via api-client
contexts.description: Lets operators browse, triage, and act on the organisation's normative standards (rules an org expects agents to follow). The StandardsBoard renders a tree of rules with a detail panel; triage helpers score incoming memories against standards; the divergence sub-surface visualises how practices across teams have drifted from declared norms using a board and matrix view.
contexts.name: standards-board

contexts.description: The entire Postgres data plane: every aggregate repository (memories, entities, governance, retrieval, documents, library standards/skills/proposals, publishing, org/identity/token management, job queue, and archive) under a strict RLS discipline. The runtime pool drops to the brainiac_app constrained role so all queries run through scoped_tx stamped with the caller's org_id/user_id; there is no unscoped read path for tenant data.
contexts.name: store-data-plane
